figures.name: temporal-knowledge-graph
figures.title: Temporal knowledge graph · implemented schema
figures.caption: Node types and allowed relationships read from backend/app/kg/store.py. Blue: personal financial entities; green: shared guidance. This is the complete allowed relationship schema, not a populated user snapshot. Every edge carries valid_from/valid_to and recorded_at/expired_at; nodes retain their current display labels.

figures.name: temporal-edge-history
figures.title: Temporal edge history · two clocks
figures.caption: Read directly from the Alice/Gym oracle in backend/tests/kg_query_fixtures.py, not a live account. All five retained edge versions are shown. Filled start / hollow end denote half-open intervals [start, end); arrows mean no recorded end, clipped at July 1 for display. Recorded timestamps are UTC (12:00 on the dated events). Old versions remain available for historical queries. v3 is corrected by v4; v5 records the June 1 closure on June 10. The $35 v2 remains the accepted January–March history.

figures.name: example-price-change
figures.title: Example 1 · explaining a subscription increase
figures.caption: Synthetic teaching example. Illustrative accepted history after a correction; intervals exclude their end date. The adjacent two-clock figure shows how a $45 report was corrected to $40. Price-change facts are supported by backend/app/kg/facts.py. How it is used: Compare dated SUBSCRIBES facts: $35 to $40 is a $5 increase. The merchant link identifies the charge. These are two valid-time versions of one relationship, not two simultaneous subscriptions.

figures.name: example-budget-context
figures.title: Example 2 · gathering context for a budget diagnosis
figures.caption: Synthetic teaching example. Amounts and entities are invented to illustrate the implemented projection and budget-context relationships. Monthly totals, limits, recurring amounts, and advice outcomes are edge values. A single dismissal does not trigger the repeated-dismissal suppression rule. How it is used: The monthly spending total ($90) exceeds the $80 limit by $10. Recurring-charge history and the prior dismissed suggestion provide context for diagnosis; the graph alone does not establish the cause or select an action.

figures.name: example-guidance-path
figures.title: Example 3 · connecting an account to sourced guidance
figures.caption: Synthetic teaching example. Alice and her account are synthetic. Green guidance nodes and their two relationships come from the current kb/graph.json snapshot; this is a demonstration of stored evidence, not a current tax-guidance verification. The account bridge follows SUBTYPE_CONCEPTS in project.py. How it is used: The account type links a personal account to a shared concept. That concept connects to a stored rule and its source, providing a retrieval path for an explanation with provenance. This is not a claim that every query traverses this exact path.

figures.name: example-temporal-snapshots
figures.title: Example 4 · the same past date, different knowledge
figures.caption: Synthetic teaching example. Three views of the SAME Alice→Gym relationship, not three users or subscriptions. Values and dates illustrate the existing Alice/Gym query-test oracle. All dates are in 2026; recording boundaries are at 12:00 UTC. Intervals exclude their end. The January knowledge view is a historical belief about April, not a guaranteed forecast. “Onward” describes what that retained version asserted at the time; the later closure is shown in the two-clock timeline. How it is used: Hold the valid date fixed at April 2 and change known_at. Before the increase was recorded, the graph returned $35. After the report it returned $45. After the correction it returned $40. Earlier versions remain queryable rather than being overwritten.
